text_to_image: First-person perspective. The protagonist is holding a small mechanical toy in one hand. Below the hand is a wooden table that fully covers the background. The toy is small enough to fit perfectly in one hand and is currently in its untransformed state. It is a compact, canted triangular ingot-shaped object made of matte black carbon fiber with polished anodized orange aluminum trim. The outer shell is completely closed, solid and seamless, with no gears, springs or moving parts visible anywhere on its surface. The toy features a circular brushed gold pressure stud mounted flush on the dorsal ridge. Soft diffused daylight from the upper left, shallow depth of field. Photorealistic, ultra-detailed, high quality.
image_to_video: First-person perspective, filmed in one continuous long take, strictly no cuts or camera transitions allowed. The camera remains steady and does not move. The protagonist presses the circular brushed gold pressure stud on the dorsal ridge with their finger, then places the toy onto the wooden table below. The transformation begins immediately and completes fully within the shot. The toy begins unfolding and transforming until it becomes the form of a miniature mechanical toco toucan. The unfolding and transformation process is logical and physically consistent. The upper triangular shell plates separate along a central spine and slide backward to form folded wings, revealing the movement of internal mechanical components and gears. An oversized brightly anodized curved bill, a keen ocular sensor, and a pair of articulated clawed feet physically push out into place. The transformation process is relatively simple and not overly complicated. Strictly no parts appear or disappear out of nowhere. After transformation, the final mechanical toco toucan's size remains believable and perfectly consistent with what the original toy could realistically unfold into, with absolutely no magical volume expansion. In the last second the finished toco toucan settles into a still pose, resting on the same spot where the closed toy was placed, and the shot holds completely steady with no further movement and nothing entering the frame, so the clip cuts back to its opening without a jolt when it loops. Audio: crisp mechanical clicks, servo whirs and ratcheting gears, ending with a soft metallic latch as the transformation completes. No music, no voice.
